AMRPA Operations Tool

Rehab Hospital Service Delivery Dashboard

Generalist vs. Specialist Model

Project Objective

Build an interactive operations model that helps rehab hospitals compare care delivery models, improve patient satisfaction, and strengthen operational effectiveness.

Current Recipe Hybrid triage model

Generalists handle routine cases; specialists support high-complexity patients and escalation paths.

Patient Satisfaction 87 Target: 90+
Avg. Length of Stay 13.2 Target: 12.5 days
Therapist Utilization 81% Target: 78-85%
Readmission Rate 8.4% Target: under 7%

Scenario Inputs

Stakeholder Map

  • Patients and familiesRecovery quality, wait time, communication, safe discharge
  • CliniciansRight patient-provider match, workload balance, outcomes
  • Operations leadersThroughput, staffing efficiency, bed utilization, cost per case
  • PayersValue, appropriate length of stay, lower readmissions
  • AMRPA membersRepeatable scenario tool and clear recommendations

Stock and Flow Diagram

AMRPA rehab hospital flow from patient-in to patient-out, with key demand and capacity drivers.

Causal loop view
Factors affecting patient-in
  • Acute care discharge
  • Proximity to AMRPA rehab hospital
  • Insurance coverage
  • Physician and hospital referrals
  • External events and demand shocks
Inflow Patient In Eligible rehab patients enter through referrals, discharge planning, and payer authorization.
Stock / Work-in-process AMRPA Rehab Hospital Patients receiving inpatient rehabilitation services before discharge.
Staff capacityClinician availability and utilization
SeverityPatient complexity and care intensity
QualityCare coordination and functional improvement
BedsPhysical capacity and occupancy
Insurance approvalAuthorization speed and coverage limits
Length of stayTime patients remain in the system
Outflow Patient Out Patient exits through safe discharge, transfer, or next-care placement.
Patient-out conditions
  • Discharge readiness
  • Functional improvement
  • Caregiver and home support
  • Post-acute follow-up plan
Capacity loop More patient-in volume raises occupancy, which strains beds and staff capacity, increasing length of stay and slowing future admissions.
Quality loop Higher care quality improves outcomes and patient satisfaction, strengthening referrals and future patient-in demand.
Insurance loop Faster insurance approval reduces admission delays and discharge friction, improving flow from patient-in to patient-out.
Severity loop Higher severity increases resource needs and length of stay, reducing available capacity unless staffing or beds increase.

Success KPI Framework

KPIWhy it mattersTarget logic
Patient satisfactionCaptures experience and perceived valueIncrease without harming access
Functional improvementMeasures clinical progress during stayImprove per patient episode
Length of stayBalances recovery time and capacityReduce only when outcomes hold
UtilizationShows staffing efficiency and bottlenecksKeep in productive range
ReadmissionsFlags discharge quality and care mismatchLower through better match quality
